verdict.rationale: Fellow offers coarse privilege tiers and agent-related controls. Users can create multiple named API keys, one per application. Key tiers are separated: user and workspace keys versus Super Admin keys that can act on behalf of any user. For MCP agent connections, admins can restrict which tools members' AI assistants may use and revoke connections, and the MCP server only exposes data the user already has access to. However, no per-key permission scopes are documented, so a least-privilege credential cannot be minted for a specific agent. Missing for 10: per-key scopes (e.g. read-only or endpoint/resource-limited keys), per-credential MCP tool scoping rather than a workspace-wide allowlist, key expiry/TTL, independent corroboration.
